root_cause.text: The STM32 ASoC SAI driver mismanaged the lifetime of the sync-provider device-tree node (`sai->np_sync_provider`) by only releasing its OF reference in `stm32_sai_set_sync()` error handling instead of on platform probe failure and driver removal, causing a leaked/stale node reference that could lead to use-after-free on reprobe.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states the sync-provider OF node reference “is currently only dropped if the set_sync() callback fails during DAI probe” and “Make sure to drop the reference on platform probe failures ... and on driver unbind,” while the patch removes `of_node_put(np_provider)` from `stm32_sai_set_sync()` and adds `of_node_put(sai->np_sync_provider)` to `stm32_sai_sub_parse_of()` failure paths, `stm32_sai_sub_probe()` error cleanup, and `stm32_sai_sub_remove()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the missing-device error path in stm32_sai_set_sync() by removing an incorrect of_node_put() on the provider node.
intent_record.what: The call to of_node_put(np_provider) was removed from the error path inside stm32_sai_set_sync() when of_find_device_by_node() fails and pdev is NULL, leaving only the dev_err() log and return -ENODEV.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents decrementing the reference count of np_provider in that failure branch, avoiding an incorrect or premature release of the device tree node that could lead to reference counting imbalance or use-after-free-related issues elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify stm32_sai_set_sync() error handling by using direct returns and removing the exit-time of_node_put() cleanup.
intent_record.what: The function stm32_sai_set_sync() was simplified by replacing two error paths that assigned or propagated ret and jumped to a shared error label with direct returns, removing the error label, deleting the of_node_put(np_provider) call from the common exit path, and returning the result of stm32_sai_sync_conf_provider(sai_provider, synco) directly.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now exits immediately on a missing sync provider or client configuration failure, and no longer calls of_node_put(np_provider) on those paths or after provider configuration. It also directly returns the provider configuration result instead of storing it in ret first. This changes cleanup behavior by eliminating the device-node reference release that previously happened on exit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route the unsupported external sync error path through common cleanup so resources are properly released before returning -EINVAL.
intent_record.what: The direct `return -EINVAL;` after `of_node_put(args.np);` in the unsupported external sync path was replaced with setting `ret = -EINVAL;` and jumping to `err_put_sync_provider` via `goto`.
intent_record.how: Instead of exiting the function immediately on this error path, execution now goes through the shared cleanup label, ensuring the sync provider reference or related resources are released before returning the invalid-argument error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the invalid SAI index error path to return through the common cleanup label and avoid leaking sync-provider resources.
intent_record.what: The direct `return -EINVAL;` in the invalid SAI index error path was replaced with `ret = -EINVAL;` followed by `goto err_put_sync_provider;` after `of_node_put(args.np);`.
intent_record.how: Instead of exiting immediately on an invalid SAI index, the function now routes execution through the shared cleanup label, ensuring any additional resources associated with the sync provider path are released before returning the error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route the unknown SAI sub-block error through the common cleanup path so sync-provider resources are properly released before returning -EINVAL.
intent_record.what: The direct `return -EINVAL;` in the `!sai->synco` error path was replaced with setting `ret = -EINVAL;` and jumping to `err_put_sync_provider` via `goto` after calling `of_node_put(args.np);`.
intent_record.how: Instead of exiting immediately, the function now routes this invalid sub-block case through the shared cleanup path, ensuring any sync-provider-related resources or references are released before returning the error code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route clock acquisition and preparation failures through the shared cleanup path so sync-provider resources are properly released on error.
intent_record.what: The error handling after devm_clk_get(&pdev->dev, "sai_ck") was changed from immediately returning dev_err_probe(...) to storing its result in ret and jumping to err_put_sync_provider; likewise, the direct return on clk_prepare(sai->pdata->pclk) failure was replaced with a jump to err_put_sync_provider.
intent_record.how: On failures when acquiring the sai_ck clock or preparing pclk, execution now follows the common error path at err_put_sync_provider instead of returning immediately, ensuring previously acquired sync-provider related resources are released before exiting.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the sync provider OF node on the parse error path to fix a device tree node reference leak.
intent_record.what: A new error-handling label, err_put_sync_provider, was added before the return path, and a call to of_node_put(sai->np_sync_provider) was inserted so that execution falling through err_unprepare_pclk now also releases the sync provider device tree node reference.
intent_record.how: On this error path, the driver now decrements the reference count of sai->np_sync_provider before returning, preventing a leaked OF node reference when parsing fails after that node has been acquired.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the sync provider device-tree node in the probe error path to fix a reference leak.
intent_record.what: A call to of_node_put(sai->np_sync_provider) was added in the err_unprepare_pclk error path of stm32_sai_sub_probe(), immediately after clk_unprepare(sai->pdata->pclk) and before returning ret.
intent_record.how: This releases the device tree node reference held in sai->np_sync_provider when probe fails along that cleanup path, preventing a leaked OF node reference during error handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the sync provider device tree node in the remove path to fix a reference leak during STM32 SAI subdevice cleanup.
intent_record.what: A call to of_node_put(sai->np_sync_provider) was added at the end of stm32_sai_sub_remove() after runtime PM is disabled.
intent_record.how: This releases the device tree node reference stored in sai->np_sync_provider during device removal, preventing the reference from being leaked and ensuring proper cleanup of resources associated with the subdevice.

grouping_result.intent: Release the sync provider device tree node in the remove path to fix a reference leak during STM32 SAI subdevice cleanup.
Route the unknown SAI sub-block error through the common cleanup path so sync-provider resources are properly released before returning -EINVAL.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix STM32 SAI sync-provider device-tree node reference management by correcting OF node cleanup across setup, probe, error, and remove paths.
Ensure all invalid or unsupported SAI configuration error paths funnel through the common cleanup label so sync-provider resources are released before returning -EINVAL.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the sync-provider OF node lifetime bug by fixing where of_node_put() is called and adding missing cleanup in probe failure, parse/error paths, and remove paths, which matches the root cause of leaked/stale node references leading to reprobe UAF risk.
The group changes error paths in sync/setup handling to use the common cleanup that releases the sync-provider OF node, directly addressing the leaked/stale reference aspect of the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This probe error-path return exits without releasing sai->np_sync_provider, matching the root cause that the OF node reference was not cleaned up on platform probe failure.
The remove path ended after this cleanup and lacked any of_node_put(sai->np_sync_provider), so driver removal leaked the sync-provider node reference and left a stale reference across reprobe.

This statement released the provider node only in stm32_sai_set_sync() error handling, embodying the mismanaged lifetime described in the root cause by tying cleanup to the wrong scope instead of probe/remove lifecycle.
This early probe failure return bypassed any cleanup of sai->np_sync_provider, contributing directly to the leaked OF node reference on probe failure.
This early return after clk_prepare failure exits probe without releasing the saved sync-provider OF node reference, consistent with the missing probe-failure cleanup.

vuln_statements.explanation: This probe error-path return exits stm32_sai_sub probe without releasing the saved sync-provider device-tree node reference in sai->np_sync_provider. That directly matches the root cause: the OF node lifetime was not cleaned up on probe failure, leading to a leaked/stale reference.

This early return on clock acquisition failure bypasses any cleanup of sai->np_sync_provider. Because probe can fail after the sync-provider node was acquired, returning here leaks that OF node reference, contributing to the stale reference issue on reprobe.

This was the end of the remove path cleanup before the fix, and no of_node_put(sai->np_sync_provider) followed it. As a result, driver removal failed to drop the sync-provider OF node reference, causing the lifetime mismatch described in the root cause.

This statement shows the incorrect lifetime management design: the provider node was only released in stm32_sai_set_sync() error handling, rather than being managed on the owning object's probe-failure and remove paths. That misplaced cleanup is the core of the reference leak/stale node bug.
